gaps.note: The reader knows dot products but not bilinear forms; the page never says that the form is <x,y> = x^T (I-J/9) y, so the reader cannot check that it gives |T∩S|-1 or what orthogonality, U^perp and projections 'along U^perp' mean afterwards.

gaps.quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
gaps.note: Nondegeneracy of a subspace with respect to a bilinear form is not in the reader's background and is not explained; the reader cannot see why it is required (it is what makes F = U ⊕ U^perp so that P_U exists).

gaps.term: the form on the tensor space F
gaps.note: The form is defined only on Q^h, but orthogonal complements and projections are taken in F = (Q^h)^{⊗3}; the page never states the induced form on F (e.g. the product of the factor forms), so U^perp, U_iota^perp and P_U in F are undefined for the reader.

gaps.term: switch from F_2 coefficients to Q labels
gaps.note: The cancellation is computed over F_2, but labels, projections and ranks are taken over Q, where the same coefficients (2 for intersections of size 1 or 2) would not cancel; the page never says how the F_2 network and the rational matrices whose ranks are counted are related.

gaps.term: label growth along a side wire
gaps.quote: Along a side wire, a label containing $t_T$ may grow to $t_S^\perp$, since $t_T\perp t_S$, adding $h-2$ dimensions.
gaps.note: The page never states the rule for how labels may change along wires, never says what a 'side wire' is, and labels live in F while t_T and t_S^perp live in Q^h; the reader cannot check why orthogonality permits the growth or where the count h-2 comes from.

gaps.quote: Let $s$, the total rank over all edges, change meaning here.
gaps.note: Nodes are given projections, but the page never says which matrix an edge carries (implicitly the difference of its endpoint projections); without that the reader cannot connect edge ranks to label dimension changes or check that the first edge out of a source has matrix 2P_{U_iota}.

gaps.quote: Each unit of rank costs one smaller call. (cited)
gaps.note: This cited claim carries the whole purpose of the construction, but the page never says what a 'smaller call' is, which recursion makes it, or why the rank of an edge matrix determines the number of calls.

The reader is not told where each wire starts and ends, what label a non-source wire starts with, why sinks have label F of dimension D, why the sinks receiving sources have label U_iota^perp, or why gate labels cancel, so the telescoping sum cannot be checked.

gaps.quote: Each of the $3\binom h3^2$ invocations has $h$ central wires
gaps.note: The page never describes how the gather/scatter construction is applied inside F (e.g. once per tensor coordinate for each choice of the other two triples), so the reader cannot check the count 3·C(h,3)^2 of invocations, or why each central wire loses exactly h dimensions on a decreasing edge.

gaps.term: fixed space and the paper's m

gaps.note: 'Fixed space' is not explained or linked, and the role of the paper's dimension m is not said, so the reader cannot see why s<WD is the inequality that matters.

gaps.quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
gaps.note: The bound's content is not stated (presumably s<Wm), nor how it makes the recursion 'save a power'; the page does not link the Recursive power saving page, so the reader cannot tell what the computation was for.
